note: WV Roofing: real manufacturers' products behind the eight looks, with specifications for material quantities (serverlib/wvroofing/catalogue.js and quantities.js). Server only: never served to browsers. Every specification here is a DRAFT, pre-filled on 2026-09-28 from the manufacturers' own published data (sources listed per product); drafts appear only on the operator screen until the roofer checks each against the datasheet and marks it verified (verified_by, verified_at). Coverage rows marked basis 'manufacturer formula' are worked out with the manufacturer's own published formula where no figure is printed for that headlap. Slate headlaps are for MODERATE exposure (under 56.5 l/m2 per spell); severe exposure needs bigger laps and more slates. The 5% default allowance follows Cupa's and Welsh Slate's advice to add at least 5% for waste; for the tiles it is WV's assumption for the roofer to confirm. Pack size 1 means counted singly; pallet quantities are given for ordering.

notes: Cupa calls CUPA 12 grey or blue-grey, not blue-black; SSQ Del Carmen (the look's other comparable) wasn't researched.
Cupa's printed coverage matches 1,000,000 ÷ (((500 − headlap) ÷ 2) × 250); the 95, 85, 70, 60 and 55 mm rows use that formula (no printed figure).
Moderate exposure. Severe exposure needs bigger headlaps: 27.5° 110 mm, 30° 100 mm, 35° 85 mm, 40° 80 mm, 45–75° 70 mm.
Conditions: at most 12 m to the eaves; rafters up to 9 m (moderate) or 6 m (severe). Hook fixing not below 25°.
Crate and pallet quantities aren't published; Cupa names no matching ridge.
